title: KMD is a Japanese-owned Danish public-sector incumbent, ruled out with no stack researched
content:
The record for KMD holds two facts and a verdict. The facts are that it is a Danish public-sector incumbent and that it is Japanese-owned; the verdict is priority 9, do not pitch. Its tool column reads not researched, so no platform, no open-source posture and no slot-occupancy assessment exist for this row.

Both recorded facts point the same way under the screen's criteria as they are applied elsewhere in the corpus. Public-sector incumbency delivers access but not partnership fit — the pattern named explicitly for the Sopra Steria entries — and ownership outside the region is treated as disqualifying even for firms with strong local benches. Neither inference is spelled out here, though, which is why this row should be read as thinly evidenced rather than firmly settled.

The practical value of the entry is as a placeholder with a known gap: if Denmark is ever worked seriously, KMD is the incumbent to understand for market context, and the first thing to do is research the stack that was never recorded.
